name: CPCRN ciprofloxacin–tamsulosin
question: Do ciprofloxacin or tamsulosin improve symptoms over placebo in men with long-standing, previously treated chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome?

design.population: 196 men with refractory chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome, an NIH-CPSI score of at least 15, mean symptom duration of 6.2 years, and substantial prior treatment.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, factorial randomized superiority trial
design.setting: 10 tertiary North American urology outpatient clinics

verdictNote: Neither factorial main effect improved the primary symptom endpoint significantly.
takeaway: In men with refractory, long-standing CP/CPPS, six weeks of ciprofloxacin, tamsulosin, both drugs, or placebo produced modest symptom-score declines; neither ciprofloxacin nor tamsulosin significantly improved the prespecified NIH-CPSI outcome over its factorial comparison.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Alexander RB, Propert KJ, Schaeffer AJ, et al. "Ciprofloxacin or Tamsulosin in Men with Chronic Prostatitis/Chronic Pelvic Pain Syndrome: A Randomized, Double-Blind Trial." *Ann Intern Med.* 2004;141(8):581-589. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-141-8-200410190-00005
reports.followUp: 6-week primary outcome; symptom follow-up at 9 and 12 weeks
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Study Design and Interventions, p 583

results.measure: Ciprofloxacin main effect on NIH-CPSI total score at 6 weeks
results.note: Treatment-by-treatment interaction was not significant (P=0.075), so the primary analysis used factorial main effects. Modeled 6-week NIH-CPSI slope: ciprofloxacin -5.4 (95% CI -6.8 to -3.9) versus no ciprofloxacin -3.9 (95% CI -5.3 to -2.4); 98 randomized per factorial group, all available observations analyzed.

results.measure: Tamsulosin main effect on NIH-CPSI total score at 6 weeks
results.note: Modeled 6-week NIH-CPSI slope: tamsulosin -4.4 (95% CI -5.8 to -2.9) versus no tamsulosin -4.8 (95% CI -6.2 to -3.3); 98 randomized per factorial group, all available observations analyzed.

results.endpoint: NIH-CPSI total score change by randomized arm
results.measure: Mean baseline-to-6-week change among participants with complete data
results.note: Completers-only descriptive means, distinct from the longitudinal primary analysis; no individual-arm superiority test was prespecified.

results.measure: Markedly or moderately improved at 6 weeks; missing responses counted as nonresponse
results.note: Intention-to-treat denominators; neither factorial comparison was statistically significant (P>0.2 for both).
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes, p 583; Tables 4-5, p 586

harms.label: Any adverse event during treatment
harms.note: Safety-evaluable after at least 3 weeks; infection or fever occurred in 1/48 placebo, 0/47 ciprofloxacin, 1/48 tamsulosin, and 0/47 combination. Overall factorial adverse-event comparisons: P>0.2 for both drugs.
harms.locator: Full text, Appendix Table, p W-111; Results, p 586

harms.label: Worst adverse-event grade
harms.value: Among 190 safety-evaluable men, grade 1 mild: 41/190 (22%); grade 2 moderate: 33/190 (17%); grade 3 severe: 2/190 (1%), one each with placebo and ciprofloxacin alone, both progression of chronic pelvic pain.
harms.note: National Cancer Institute Common Toxicity Criteria grading, not Clavien-Dindo.
harms.locator: Full text, Outcomes, p 583; Results, p 586

delivery.label: Drug regimen
delivery.value: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg once daily, both drugs, or placebo for 6 weeks.
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1; Study Design and Interventions, pp 582-583

delivery.label: Six-week follow-up and treatment completion
delivery.value: 174/196 (89%) had a 6-week outcome; 17/196 (9%) withdrew before week 6 and 5/196 missed that clinic visit. Eleven patients stopped treatment early but continued follow-up and were included in analyses.
